correctness.rationale: Disjoint nonempty odd-valuation sets give a geometrically connected biquadratic cover, with eight tame inertia-two branches, hence genus five. The nontrivial characters give the two elliptic quotients and the common genus-three quotient uv(x⁷−x). In F49 the image of x⁷−x is the seven-element trace-zero line, whose nonzero elements satisfy w^24=1 and are squares. This gives 92 points on the quotient over F49 and forces each squared Weil eigenvalue to be −7; conjugate multiplicities give (1+7T²)³. The quartets have two anharmonic orbits of cross ratios of sizes 3 and 2, giving 42 and 28 quartets by sharp three-transitivity and division by 24. Complementation is equivariant and preserves these two different-sized orbits. The respective representative Legendre traces are 0 and 4; twisting independently gives 84 zero pairs, 14 of each same-sign nonzero pair, and 28 mixed pairs. The displayed extension-field counts, 7-ranks and elliptic splitting follow from the quotient decomposition and finite-field isogeny by Frobenius polynomial for the trace-zero factor. Independent direct normalization-fiber counts over both fields for all 140 marked models agree (include the infinity fiber); this is a check of the finite census, not a substitute for the quotient proof of the full zeta polynomials.
residual_risks: The frozen proof does not count abstract curve isomorphism classes or prove a polarization decomposition; its table counts marked models only.
